subject: New to R/qtl... a question about markers on the X chromosome

messages.author: aa237e73fd5c701a
messages.subject: New to R/qtl... a question about markers on the X chromosome
parts:
Hi,

I ran into a problem that I was not able to address using the help
files or bugging the people in the lab next door. As a first trial, I
am running a QTL analysis with just four markers (coded as 0,1,
Drosophila visible markers) on the X chromosome on a population of
backcross males (XY). I am not sure how to indicate the genotype, and
it seems that setting it up in different ways yields significantly
different results. Does somebody know what is the correct way of doing
this? I tried it as AA and AB, and also as AA and BB. First
arrangement indicates they are all females, seocnd that they are all
males... yet in the summary both arrangements disclose the genotypes as
ony AA or AB. I am confused.... Thanks!!

M

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: New to R/qtl... a question about markers on the X chromosome
parts:
Code them as AA/BB, and include a phenotype "sex", with all 1's.
(or M's). And make sure that you call the chromosomes "X".

If the genotypes are being called AA/AB in the software,
ignore that. Or maybe check that you are using the latest version.
I thought that was now fixed.

karl

messages.subject: Re: New to R/qtl... a question about markers on the X chromosome
parts:
Hi Karl et al.,
Forgive me for resurrecting this ancient thread... but I'm experiencing similar problems trying to load X chromosome genotypes for an F2 intercross, males only (which are hemizygous). Specifically, the software continues to recode my genotypes as AA/AB. So far I've tried:

1. Coding genotypes as A/B
2. Coding genotypes as A/B, adding "sex" column with all individuals coded as "1"
3. Coding genotypes as AA/BB, "sex" column with all individuals coded as "1", and including "genotypes" and "alleles" arguments in read.cross

In each case, read.cross seems to finish normally, and it identifies the appropriate cross type (F2). But when I execute summary.cross it reports only AA and AB at the "Genotypes (%):" line.

My question is whether this is simply a problem with the summary.cross function (in which case I can proceed with my analysis)? 

And yes--using the latest version of r/qtl.

Many thanks in advance for any suggestions.

Regards,
Kevin

karl
